chunks: And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: A Muslim is a brother to a Muslim
he does not betray him, nor desert him, nor disparage him, nor deprive him, nor backbite him.

key_terms.أَخُو الْمُسْلِمِ: brother to the Muslim (indicating close bond)

ai.seo_question: What are the five main rights of a Muslim upon another Muslim according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Kitab al-Mumin* by Husayn ibn Sa'id al-Ahwazi, this hadith is transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) from the Prophet (PBUH), highlighting the comprehensive nature of brotherhood (*ukhuwwah*) in Shia jurisprudence. It expands the concept of social rights beyond mere non-aggression to include active protection against psychological harm, such as backbiting (*ghibah*) and finding fault (*u'yub*), thereby establishing a holistic code of conduct for communal harmony.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 98. It has been reported that Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) said: The Prophet (a.s) said: A Muslim is a brother to the other Muslim;
he must not betray him, desert him, disgrace him, excommunicate him nor backbite him.
